meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Common feminine noun meaning 'number, figure, digit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что это за маленькие цифры в отчёте?
examples.trans: What are these small numbers in the report?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'report', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Now I will check the reports.

examples.text: Шеф, наш разведчик вернулся с отчётом.
examples.trans: Chef, our scout has returned with a report.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'little'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not enough, too little') (Это мало = That's not enough) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('few, not many') (+ genitive: мало людей) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Подождите! Два дня — это же очень мало.
examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next to'.
Secondary conversational sense ('nearby, close by') (adverb of place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.
Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

открыться.gloss: to open, to come to light

meanings.en: to come to light, to be revealed
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to open', forming an aspectual pair with 'открываться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to open') (intransitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: New circumstances have come to light.

examples.text: Прошу внимания. Открылись новые обстоятельства по другому делу.
examples.trans: May I have your attention. New circumstances have come to light in another case.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Relational Russian adjective in '-ский' meaning 'Italian', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: We went to an Italian restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to

examples.trans: The cook feeds the guests a delicious lunch.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'decision' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('solution') (to a problem) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I am forced to cancel my decision.
We have already made a decision.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
